title: MoDiff – Graph Generation with Motif-aware Diffusion Model

problem.claim: Temporal graph research faces data accessibility and privacy challenges, motivating surrogate graph generation for sharing and training.

gap.claim: Existing deep learning and probabilistic graph generation approaches struggle to balance global statistical properties with local structural details.

contributions.claim: MoDiff is a motif-aware diffusion model for temporal graph generation based on spectral analysis of motifs.
The model uses motif-enhanced Hermitian matrices to capture local structures and edge orientations within a spectral diffusion framework.
MoDiff supports controllable temporal graph generation by adjusting density parameters to simulate graph evolution.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present MoDiff as a novel motif-aware diffusion model for temporal graph generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MoDiff reduces degree discrepancies by 10–50% compared with existing approaches.
The authors report that MoDiff reduces clustering discrepancies by 50–90% compared with existing approaches.
The authors report better preservation of higher-order structural features.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal graphs are valuable but difficult to access because of privacy and data-sharing constraints.

Surrogate graph generation could support sharing, training, behavior analysis, anomaly detection, and data augmentation, but existing methods do not adequately preserve both global and local structure.
MoDiff incorporates motif information into spectral diffusion through motif-enhanced Hermitian matrices.
The method enables controllable temporal graph evolution through density parameters.
The authors report improved discrepancy measures and preservation of higher-order structural features relative to existing approaches.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation protocol, or statistical significance of the reported comparisons.
The abstract does not detail the diffusion process, motif selection, density-parameterization procedure, or temporal evolution settings.
